issues.legal_issue: An appeal against a surplus-land determination abates when the determination requires reassessment under the amended statutory scheme and the appeal remains pending at the transition specified by the transitory provision.
material_facts: The prescribed authority determined surplus land before the later amendment commenced.
An appeal against that determination was pending immediately before the transition date specified in the later amendment.
The intervening amendments replaced the earlier method of determining surplus land and required reassessment under the new scheme.
issues.conclusion: The pending appeal was deemed to have abated, and the appellate authority lacked jurisdiction to decide it on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 31(2) of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings (Amendment) Act, 1976, an appeal pending at the specified transition date against a determination made before January 17, 1975 abates where the prescribed authority is required to redetermine surplus land under Section 9 of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings (Amendment) Act, 1974. The Court held that the amended scheme replaced the prior scheme and required redetermination. State of Uttar Pradesh v. Mithilesh Kumari and Mansoor Ali Khan v. State of U.P. were cited but held to have no direct application.

rule.if: ceiling_appeal and determination_under_superseded_scheme and redetermination_required and appeal_pending_at_transition

predicates.ceiling_appeal: A party appealed a determination of surplus land in a ceiling proceeding.
predicates.determination_under_superseded_scheme: The prescribed authority determined surplus land under a scheme that was later replaced.
predicates.redetermination_required: The amended scheme required the prescribed authority to determine surplus land afresh.
predicates.appeal_pending_at_transition: The appeal remained pending immediately before the statutory transition.

issues.definition: When a ceiling appeal challenges a determination under a superseded scheme, redetermination is required, and the appeal is pending at the transition, the appeal abates.

issues.legal_issue: The power to redetermine surplus land under the amended scheme is mandatory when an earlier determination falls within the statutory conditions for redetermination.
material_facts: The prescribed authority made its determination before the 1974 amendment commenced.
That amendment introduced a substantially different scheme for determining surplus land.
The 1976 amendment also provided for redetermination of determinations made before its specified cutoff.
issues.conclusion: The prescribed authority had no discretion to avoid redetermination in a case meeting the statutory conditions.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the word “may” in Section 9 of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings (Amendment) Act, 1974, and Section 31(3) of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings (Amendment) Act, 1976, in context. Because the new scheme replaced the former scheme, redetermination was required in every qualifying case; “may” did not confer discretion to decline it. No earlier case was relied on for this interpretation.

predicates.ceiling_redetermination: A prescribed authority is dealing with a redetermination of surplus land in a ceiling proceeding.
predicates.prior_determination_under_replaced_schem: The prescribed authority previously determined surplus land under a scheme that was replaced.
predicates.amended_scheme_applies: The amended scheme governs the earlier determination and requires a fresh determination.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding concerns an earlier determination under a replaced scheme and the amended scheme applies, the authority must redetermine surplus land.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a fresh notice was issued does not determine whether an otherwise qualifying appeal abates under the later transitory provision.
material_facts: The appellate authority and the High Court treated the absence of a fresh notice as a reason the proceedings had not abated.
The Supreme Court held that abatement under the later transitory provision depended on its statutory conditions, not on whether a fresh notice had been issued.
The record was also found to show that a fresh notice had in fact been issued.
issues.conclusion: The issuance or non-issuance of a fresh notice did not affect abatement under Section 31; the qualifying appeal had abated.
issues.legal_principle: Section 31 of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings (Amendment) Act, 1976, governed abatement by reference to the specified prior determination, required redetermination, and pending appeal. The Court held that issuance of a notice under Section 9(2) of the 1972 amendment was not an additional condition for abatement.

predicates.qualifying_ceiling_appeal: A party appealed a surplus-land determination in a ceiling proceeding, and the appeal falls within the statutory transition conditions for abatement.
predicates.statutory_transition_conditions_met: The determination requires redetermination under the amended scheme and the appeal was pending at the relevant transition.

issues.definition: When a ceiling appeal meets the transition conditions for abatement, whether a fresh notice was issued does not control that abatement.

issues.legal_issue: The earlier transitory provision did not prevent a fresh determination where the prescribed authority issued the required new notice and the earlier surplus-land determination had not become final before the amended scheme commenced.
material_facts: Proceedings under the earlier scheme were pending when the 1972 amendment commenced.
A general notice under the amended notice procedure was issued, and the tenure-holder did not respond to it.
The earlier surplus-land determination had not become final through disposal of an appeal before the amended scheme commenced.
issues.conclusion: The earlier transitory provision did not invalidate the fresh proceedings or the resulting determination on the basis asserted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 19(1) of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings (Amendment) Act, 1972, provided for pending proceedings to abate and fresh proceedings to begin by notice under Section 9(2). Section 19(2) preserved specified proceedings only where surplus land had been finally determined before commencement. The Court held that the fresh notice had been given and that the earlier determination had not become final before commencement.

predicates.ceiling_proceeding_under_amended_scheme: An authority proceeded to determine surplus land under an amended ceiling scheme.
predicates.fresh_notice_issued: The prescribed authority issued a new notice calling for a statement under the amended procedure.
predicates.earlier_determination_not_final: The earlier surplus-land determination had not become final before the amended scheme commenced.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding under an amended scheme follows a fresh notice and the earlier determination was not final, the prior transition does not invalidate the fresh determination.
